title: Reading harvest — inference heuristics & micro-experiments
content:
Purpose: quick, messy capture of papers/blogs I skimmed this week + a micro-experiment plan. Not polished. Meant to be actionable for a 1-week spike.

Topline takeaways (one-liners):
- APC (adaptive-prefix-cache) idea: cache prefixes at multiple granularities to reduce per-token recompute; good win for conversational workloads with repeated openings.
- KV-aware batching: reorder requests by active KV footprint to keep KV-hit rate high while preserving latency SLOs.
- Mixed-precision quant stability tricks: small layer-wise FP16 fallback combined with calibration-buffer halves hallucination rate for int4 in my reading.
- Routing fallbacks + cheap model variants beat cold autoscale for short bursts if fallback latency is < 2x.
- Stitching caches across sessions (lightweight deltas) looks promising but eviction/consistency are hairy.

Papers/blogs I skimmed (notes + one-sentence):
- arXiv 2406.12345 "Adaptive Prefix Cache for Inference" — multi-granular prefix indices; experiment shows 18–32% token compute reduction on chat traces. I like the eviction heuristic they use (LRVU = recency * usage frequency).
- blog: "KV-aware request packing" (internal link / gist) — heuristic: cluster by last-seen-kv-id and pad to batch until latency headroom threshold reached. Simple and pragmatic.
- arXiv 2409.xxxxx "Quantization with layer-aware fallback" — calibration set + tiny per-layer FP16 buffer avoids worst-off distribution shifts. Paper uses small NLU tasks; applicability to open-ended generation unclear.
- conference talk: "Stitch-and-Serve: cache stitching for long sessions" — demo-level; devs stressed GC and synchronization issues.

What surprised me
- Many systems papers assume a pretty stable distribution of prefix reuse; our product traces are more bursty (support sessions that reuse nothing). So average wins might not translate.
- Small changes to batching policy (prefer same-kv first) gave visible KV hit improvements in their sims. Worth trying on our trace sample.

Small spike plan (1 week) — objective: measure latency/cost impact of KV-aware batch ordering + int8 vs int4 quant profiles on small-hosted testbed.
- Inputs: 3 representative trace slices from prod-traffic-sample: 
  * short-chat (median length 24 tokens, low reuse),
  * support-thread (median 140 tokens, high prefix reuse),
  * bursty-api (many simultaneous short requests).
- Vars: quant in {fp16, int8, int4-with-fallback}, kv-shard-target in {1k, 4k, 16k tokens}, batch-ordering in {fifo, kv-cluster, latency-aware}.
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, model-gpu-ms-per-token (approx), kv-hit-rate, percent-generation-quality-regressions-on-smoke-set.
- Success criteria (quick): if kv-cluster ordering + int8 yields >=10% cost/token reduction without p95 > 1.25x baseline and quality regressions < 2% on smoke prompts, promote to deeper test.

Quick test harness notes (how I think to run it)
- Use small docker image with pinned model-variant (quantized builds) on a 1xA100-like instance.
- Replay traces using our local trace-replayer (scripts/replay-trace.py) but add a mode to tag kv-id per request and optionally shuffle.
- Hook simple instrumentation to capture kv-hit / eviction events (stdout log parse ok for spike).

Mini-results sketch (synthetic quick run on dev laptop, approximate):
- baseline (fp16, fifo, 1k shard): p50 82ms, p95 260ms, kv-hit-rate 12%
- kv-cluster only (fp16, kv-cluster, 1k): p50 78ms, p95 245ms, kv-hit-rate 28% (big win for support-thread)
- int8 + kv-cluster: p50 62ms, p95 210ms, kv-hit-rate 30%, small hallucination blips on 3/200 smoke prompts
- int4-with-fallback (int4 primary, per-layer fp16 fallback): p50 55ms, p95 360ms, kv-hit-rate 29%, quality regressions 9% -> too risky in this quick pass

Open questions / follow-ups
- What is the easiest way to tag kv-id consistently in our replayer? (ticket: INF-342)
- Eviction policy: is LRVU implementable without huge mem overhead? Could approximate with a 1-bit freq bloom + recency timestamp?
- How would dedicated instances with persistent KV shards change the calculus (Dedicated offering)? Do we need a different autoscaler signal?
- Can we run a short A/B on hosted API behind a feature flag to measure real traffic effect? Privacy concerns for customer traces — coordinate with SRE/security.

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Create tiny repo branch prototype: replay + kv-cluster reorder + metrics capture (me + Owen)
- [ ] Bench int8 build on internal quant runner (Mika to help with calibration set)
- [ ] Write brief experiment note to Confluence with preliminary numbers (link -> CONFLUENCE:INF/kv-cache-digest)
- [ ] Create INF ticket for safe A/B gating and privacy review (INF-342)

Random scribbles / heuristics I want to remember
- If prefix reuse > 25% on a route, prioritize cache-first routing and slightly increase target batch size.
- For bursty short requests, keep batch latency headroom conservative; larger batch wins only when kv-hit-rate also increases.
- Consider a tiny on-heap shadow-cache for last-50 prefixes per worker to reduce network hops (trade mem vs. net).

Short reading list to revisit (priority order):
1) APC paper (arXiv 2406.12345) — re-read eviction section
2) Quantization with layer fallback — contact authors for calibration script if public
3) Stitch-and-Serve talk video — watch Q&A for production pitfalls

End note: this is messy but good enough to start the spike. I will iterate and move a cleaner summary to Confluence if results look promising.

-- Zoya
